data.content_ref: inline:The mechanism is physically inverted: drier (less humid) air has LOWER atmospheric longwave emissivity and therefore emits LESS downwelling longwave radiation toward the surface. With less downwelling longwave offsetting surface emission, the surface would lose net energy FASTER and cool MORE, not slower. Thus reduced humidity cannot 'slow radiative cooling' via 'lowered longwave emissivity' — the sign is backwards. A slower nocturnal cooling rate in drier air is opposite to observed physics; the target's premise contradicts the mechanism it invokes.
